summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would create stronger governance and financial transparency rules for unions and employer associations.
It would set up a new body called the Registered Organisations Commission to monitor these groups and investigate wrongdoing.
The commissioner would have powers similar to those of the Australian Securities and Investments Commission under the Corporations Act 2001.
changes: Establishes the Registered Organisations Commission as an independent regulator.
Requires officers to disclose material personal interests and restricts their voting and decision-making rights.
Increases civil penalties and creates criminal offences for serious breaches of officers' duties.
Strengthens financial accounting, disclosure and transparency obligations by making rule obligations enforceable as civil remedy provisions.
summary.affected: Registered organisations, their branches and their officers.

divisions.question: Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment Bill 2014 - Second Reading - Agree to bill's main idea

speeches.speaker: Brendan O'Connor
speeches.brief: Opposed the Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment Bill 2014, noting it sets a maximum penalty of $85,000 for an officer who fails to respond within 28 days to a member's request, compared with the Corporations Act's maximum of $200,000 for individuals and $1 million for companies in equivalent serious contraventions.

speeches.speaker: Natasha Griggs
speeches.brief: Supported the Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment Bill 2014, citing Michael Williamson's guilty plea to misusing almost $1 million in Health Services Union funds, and detailed a Northern Territory commission of inquiry finding against former Labor ministers Delia Lawrie and Gerry McCarthy over a lease granted to Unions NT.

speeches.speaker: Adam Bandt
speeches.brief: Opposed the Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment Bill 2014 as part of a broader attack on workers' rights, warning that new rules letting employers pay in kind could see a fish and chip shop worker paid partly in food, unable to cover rent or electricity bills.

speeches.speaker: Julie Owens
speeches.brief: Opposed the Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment Bill 2014, arguing the Health Services Union prosecution of 181 rule breaches proved existing laws already work, and drew on her nearly seven years running the Australian Independent Record Labels Association, representing about 80 per cent of the sector, to argue employer bodies play the same protective role as unions.

speeches.speaker: Julie Owens
speeches.brief: Opposed the Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment Bill 2014, noting Labor's 2012 reforms already tripled penalties for registered organisation breaches, and quoted the Australian Industry Group's warning that the government's proposed criminal penalties would deter volunteers from serving as officers of employer and union bodies.

speeches.speaker: Dennis Jensen
speeches.brief: Supported Fair Work amendments curbing union right-of-entry powers, citing 676 right-of-entry visits recorded at BHP's Worsley alumina plant in 2010 alone, and quoted former AWU secretary Paul Howes warning that ignoring union dishonesty would let it 'grow like a cancer'.

speeches.speaker: Scott Buchholz
speeches.brief: Supported the Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment Bill 2014, noting it responds to 53 recommendations from a 2012 Fair Work Act review panel of John Edwards, Michael Moore and Ron McCallum, and rejected claims of coalition hostility to unions by describing his own cooperative dealings with union representatives in the transport sector.

speeches.speaker: Terri Butler
speeches.brief: Opposed the Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment Bill 2014, defending greenfields agreements by contrasting them with the Work Choices era when employers could negotiate agreements with themselves, and quoted Justice Logan's ruling in CFMEU v North Goonyella Coal Mine invoking the 1834 Tolpuddle Martyrs case to explain the historical legitimacy of trade unions.

speeches.speaker: Lisa Chesters
speeches.brief: Opposed the Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment Bill 2014, naming volunteer union officials such as part-time Spotless cleaner Marie Angrilli and V/Line conductor Bob Bassett who would face the same penalties as paid union bosses, and quoted a Herald Sun editorial criticising the government for cutting parliamentary cleaners' wages by up to $5 an hour.

speeches.speaker: Shayne Neumann
speeches.brief: Opposed the Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment Bill 2014, detailing Labor's 2012 reforms requiring registered organisations to disclose the remuneration of their five highest-paid officers and two highest-paid branch officers to members and the Fair Work Commission by 31 December each year.

speeches.speaker: Warren Snowdon
speeches.brief: Opened his remarks on the Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment Bill 2014 by praising the member for Blair's contribution, and noted he was one of the longest-serving members on the Labor side of the chamber.

speeches.speaker: Warren Snowdon
speeches.brief: Opposed the Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment Bill establishing a Registered Organisations Commissioner with investigative powers exceeding company directors' obligations, noting Labor's own 2012 reforms already require officers to disclose interests and related-party payments, and accused the NT's CLP government of far greater corruption through its Foundation 51 slush fund.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Giles
speeches.brief: Opposed the reintroduced Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment Bill as unnecessary duplication of Labor's 2012 reforms, noting the Senate had already rejected an earlier version in May, and argued its penalties exceed those in the Corporations Act despite the government's promise to align registered organisation and company regulation.

speeches.speaker: Joanne Ryan
speeches.brief: Opposed the Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment Bill, accusing the government of misusing the word 'fair' while pursuing unfair pension, education and GP tax changes, and recalled students she taught being paid in pizzas and denied overtime under the Howard government's WorkChoices laws.

speeches.speaker: Joanne Ryan
speeches.brief: Raised concerns about the Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment Bill 2014, citing the Australian Industry Group's warning that its new criminal and financial penalties would deter people from volunteering for registered organisations, and noted Labor had already tripled penalties and strengthened transparency laws for unions in 2012.

speeches.speaker: Joanne Ryan
speeches.brief: Opposed the Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment Bill as an ideological attack on unions, arguing it imposes harsher penalties on union officers than company directors face, and recalled WorkChoices-era cases including Optus contractors facing $300 a week pay cuts and $12,000 van costs.

speeches.speaker: Dan Tehan
speeches.brief: Supported the Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment Bill for greater transparency, citing the Victorian construction industry royal commission's allegations of nepotism, blackmail and cartel behaviour against the CFMEU, and criticised Labor for not distancing itself from the union.

speeches.speaker: Christopher Pyne
speeches.brief: Closed debate on the Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment Bill, explaining the new Registered Organisations Commission would both educate officials on their duties and prosecute deliberate noncompliance, with penalty provisions modelled on the Corporations Act.
